name: metis
description: Métis skills for Quality Engineering against a behaviour knowledge graph. 39 skills across the pipeline: business-analyst reads a half-formed intent from four directions before anything is landed — is there a need, can its wording be satisfied twice, could anything test it, does anybody know what being wrong costs; intake-processor and knowledge-capture bring in what somebody SAYS the system should do; model-build recovers what it ACTUALLY does from a code property graph; behavior-modeling checks the machine is well-formed; review-assist walks a human through the G1 approval gate; test-design decides what to test and how across seven specialists, reporting `incomplete` rather than a finished design when nobody has said what the architecture is; test-generate turns an approved model into human-executable cases and stops at G2; coverage-report says what is covered and — the part that makes the rest safe to read — what could not be measured; change-impact shows what a diff puts at risk before it merges; spec-writeback puts the generated specification where the team already reads; and risk-manager runs the risk lifecycle across fourteen specialists, where a risk Métis derived from a model is never merged with one a person asserted, and a requirement or release assessment reports `incomplete` rather than a clean bill when nobody has answered what only a person can. Every skill proposes; nothing approves.
